[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The scale-set Helm release can start runner workloads, but it has no dependency on the EKS Pod Identity association that grants credentials to its service account. Ensure the association is created before the release can launch workloads.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Runner pods deployed by this Helm release use EKS Pod Identity, but the identity association can otherwise be created concurrently with the release. Ensure the association exists before the chart can start workloads.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The scale-set Helm release may create runner workloads that use EKS Pod Identity, but it does not wait for the Pod Identity association. Ensure the association exists before installing the release so workloads do not start before their identity mapping is established.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set creates runner pods that assume the runner IAM role via EKS Pod Identity. aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity must exist before the scale set's pods start, otherwise runners launch without IAM credentials and fail AWS API calls (e.g. pulling from ECR). There is no attribute reference between the release and the association (the values only reference the role ARN), so the release should depend on the association.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The runner scale set helm_release only references aws_iam_role.runner_role.arn (through its values), but the runner pods it deploys rely on aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity for their AWS credentials: per the AWS docs, pods using the associated service account get Pod Identity credentials injected, which the runners need for AWS API access (e.g. ECR pulls). The helm release has no dependency on the association, so the runners can be installed before the association exists and come up without IAM credentials. The chart's async install means there is no attribute reference that would order this naturally, so an explicit depends_on is the appropriate fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity injects IAM credentials into pods using service account var.service_account in namespace var.namespace — the exact pods created by the gha_runner_scale_set Helm release. Per the AWS documentation, pods only receive credentials if the association exists. The helm_release references the IAM role ARN but not the association, so on a fresh apply the runner/listener pods can start before credentials are available and never pick them up until restarted. The release must depend on the association.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The scale-set Helm release is configured to use the runner service account, which this module creates separately, but it has no dependency on that service account. Ensure the service account exists before installing the release.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Helm release can deploy runner workloads using this service account before its Kubernetes service account exists. Make the release depend on the service-account resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The scale-set Helm release can create runner workloads that use this service account, but its namespace is currently configured only from a variable and does not order creation of the service account. Derive the Helm namespace from the account so the account exists before the release is applied.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set creates runner pods that run under the service account pre-created by kubernetes_service_account_v1.runner_sa (referenced only by name via the service_account variable in the chart values, so Terraform cannot infer ordering). On a fresh apply the scale set could be installed before the ServiceAccount exists, causing the runner/listener pods to fail to schedule. The release should depend on the ServiceAccount.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set installs the runner scale set whose pods run as the service account "runner_sa" (referenced by name via var.service_account in the chart values). If the release is applied before the Kubernetes service account exists, the listener deployment/runner pods will fail to schedule with a "serviceaccount not found" error, even though the Helm release itself reports success. The release must be ordered after the service account, but no attribute reference or depends_on expresses this.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The cleanup CronJob can begin running with its service account before the RoleBinding granting that account permissions exists. Add an ordering dependency so the job cannot run until the binding is established.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The cleanup CronJob runs with the zombie-runner service account and needs the permissions granted by this RoleBinding. Without ordering, a scheduled job could start before those permissions are in place.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The zombie cleanup CronJob can run as soon as it is created, but its Kubernetes RoleBinding may still be pending because the CronJob has no dependency on it. Order CronJob creation after the binding so the first scheduled cleanup run has the required RBAC permissions.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The scale-set Helm release can launch runner workloads that use the IAM role, but it has no dependency on the managed policy attachments for that role. If those attachments are created concurrently, workloads may start before their required permissions are attached.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The runner Helm release may start workloads that assume this role before its managed policies have been attached, leaving the runners without their intended AWS permissions during startup. Ensure the policy attachment completes before deploying the release.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The scale-set Helm release can start runner workloads using this IAM role while managed policy attachments are still being applied. Order the release after the role policy attachment so runner workloads do not start before the role's configured permissions are attached.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup` is created in `var.controller_config.namespace`, a Kubernetes namespace provisioned by `module.controller` (`kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace`). But this resource has no implicit or explicit dependency on `:module.controller`, so on a fresh apply Terraform may try to create the ServiceAccount before the namespace exists, causing "namespace not found" errors. It should depend on `:module.controller`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup is created in var.controller_config.namespace, the namespace provisioned by module.controller (kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace). It has no dependency on module.controller, so Terraform may try to create this ServiceAccount before the namespace exists and fail with "namespace not found". It should wait for module.controller.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.kubernetes_role_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup` lives in the controller namespace `var.controller_config.namespace`, which is created by `module.controller`'s `kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace`. It has no dependency (direct or transitive) on `:module.controller`, so it can be applied before the namespace exists. It should depend on `:module.controller`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_role_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup is created in var.controller_config.namespace (provisioned by module.controller) and its rule targets the actions.github.com/ephemeralrunners CRD that the controller's Helm release installs. Without a dependency on module.controller it can be applied before the namespace/CRDs exist.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.kubernetes_role_binding_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup` is a Kubernetes object in the controller namespace `var.controller_config.namespace`, created by `module.controller`. Its only dependencies are other zombie resources and variables, none of which reach `:module.controller`, so the namespace may not exist when it is created. It should depend on `:module.controller`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_role_binding_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup lives in var.controller_config.namespace, which is created by module.controller, but it only depends on the sibling SA/Role resources in the root module and never on module.controller. It can therefore be applied before the namespace (and controller CRDs) exist.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.kubernetes_cron_job_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup` is created in the controller namespace and its script queries `actions.github.com/ephemeralrunners` CRs, both of which are provided by `module.controller` (the namespace plus the controller Helm release's CRDs). It has no dependency on `:module.controller`, so on a fresh apply the namespace/CRDs may not exist yet and the CronJob will fail. It should depend on `:module.controller`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_cron_job_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup runs in var.controller_config.namespace and relies on the actions.github.com/ephemeralrunners CRD installed by module.controller's Helm release, but has no dependency on module.controller. It can race ahead of the namespace/CRD creation and fail.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity binds the runner IAM role to the service account named by var.service_account, but it only references the variable string, not the kubernetes_service_account_v1.runner_sa resource that actually creates that service account. This leaves the association and the service account with no ordering/consistency link. Wire the association's service_account to the runner_sa resource so the dependency is inferred.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity binds the service account kubernetes_service_account_v1.runner_sa to the IAM role, but references the SA only by the var.service_account string and therefore has no ordering dependency on the SA resource. Point service_account at the SA resource so the association is created after the service account exists.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup is created in namespace var.controller_config.namespace, but that namespace is only created by the scale_set_controller module (resource.kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace, under the same migrate_arc_cluster == false condition). On a fresh apply the ServiceAccount can be applied before the namespace exists, failing the apply with a 404. It should depend on the namespace resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The zombie-runner-cleanup service account (and the Role/RoleBinding/CronJob that reference it) is created in var.controller_config.namespace, but nothing orders it after that namespace is actually created. In module.controller the namespace is provisioned by kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace (and, for the controller chart, via create_namespace = true on the helm release). The zombie-runner-cleanup resources have no attribute reference to any of these, so on a fresh apply the service account can race the namespace creation and fail with a "namespace not found" API error. An explicit depends_on on the controller's namespace resource closes this gap; the Role, RoleBinding, and CronJob are transitively ordered behind the service account, so the dependency only needs to be added once.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup (and the role/role-binding/cron-job that reference it) are created in namespace var.controller_config.namespace, which is provisioned by module.controller's kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace (and otherwise only by the controller helm_release's create_namespace=true). Nothing ties the root-module zombie resources to that namespace resource, so on a fresh apply Terraform may attempt to create the service account before the namespace exists and fail with "namespaces \"arc\" not found". An ordering dependency on the controller namespace is missing.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set deploys the runner scale set whose listener consumes the hook-extension ConfigMap (hook-extension-<scale_set_name>, provided by the chart's listener hook mechanism by naming convention). If the release is installed before kubernetes_config_map.hook_extension exists, the listener starts without the hook extension and the container-podspec overrides are silently not applied until a later listener restart. The release should depend on the ConfigMap.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The runner scale set Helm chart consumes the hook ConfigMaps ("hook-extension-<scale_set_name>" and "hook-pre-post-job-<scale_set_name>") created by kubernetes_config_map.hook_extension and kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job. The helm_release only references var.scale_set_name/var.service_account strings in its values template, so Terraform may install the release before these ConfigMaps exist, leaving the runners without their hook configuration. An ordering dependency on both ConfigMaps is missing.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set deploys the runner scale set whose listener consumes the pre/post-job hook scripts from the ConfigMap named hook-pre-post-job-<scale_set_name> by convention. If the release is installed before kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job exists, the job-started/job-completed hooks are not picked up when the listener is created. The release should depend on the ConfigMap.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
Same as hook_extension: the "job_started.sh"/"job_completed.sh" hook scripts in kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job must exist before the gha_runner_scale_set Helm release is installed, otherwise the runner pods reference hook ConfigMaps that don't exist yet. No attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering.
